I’m 61 years old and only started farming two years ago when my son left to work in a factory in Handan. It’s mostly me and my wife managing the 7.7 mu now, so I can’t do everything by hand and I hire machine services when I need them. I don’t know all the book knowledge, but I watch what my neighbors like Old Wang do, and I follow them because they have good harvests. For wheat this winter, I’ll rotary till the land in October, plant the improved seed from the local cooperative, put down compound fertilizer as a base and topdress with urea in spring, irrigate three times from our well, and spray herbicide and maybe fungicide about three times total. For summer maize, the window after wheat harvest is too tight to till, so I’ll hire the no‑till planter to put hybrid seed straight into the wheat stubble, use one application of maize formula fertilizer plus a side‑dressing when the plants are knee‑high, irrigate twice if the summer rains are short, and spray twice for weeds and corn borer. I’m a bit cash‑constrained with only 7.7 mu and my son’s wages aren’t always steady, so I keep inputs moderate rather than pushing for the maximum. I expect about 480 kg per mu for wheat and 520 kg per mu for maize if the weather is normal — last year I got a bit less, but I’m learning.
